title: Painting Walls and Facades in a Tropical Climate
meta: When to repaint your Sanur villa, which paints handle sea spray and monsoon rain, and how to prep old plaster properly so the job actually lasts.
intro: Repainting a villa in Sanur is not the same as doing it in a temperate city. The salt air off the Indian Ocean, two distinct seasons, and humidity that never really drops below 70 % will peel cheap paint within a year if you skip the right steps. Below is a practical walkthrough covering timing, product choice, surface prep, moisture control, and realistic drying windows.

sections.h2: When Is the Right Time to Paint?
paragraphs: The short answer: dry season, roughly May through September. You want at least five consecutive days without rain before you start, because water trapped under fresh paint causes blistering and premature peeling. In Sanur the sea breeze helps surfaces dry faster than inland areas, but it also carries salt particles that can settle on wet coats. Aim for early morning or late afternoon application when the wind is calmer.

Avoid painting during the rainy season (October–April) unless you are working inside a fully enclosed room with dehumidification. Even a light drizzle on a freshly painted facade can ruin an entire day's work.
bullets: Check the local forecast for at least 48 hours of no-rain before scheduling exterior work.
Start interior rooms first so dust and drips do not land on finished exterior walls.
If you must paint in shoulder months (April or October), keep a tarpaulin ready and stop immediately if clouds build over the ocean.

paragraphs: For exterior walls exposed to the sea, look for acrylic- or siloxane-based paints specifically labelled for tropical or marine environments. These form a flexible film that breathes, letting moisture escape while blocking UV degradation. Standard emulsion paints from a hardware store will chalk and fade within one or two wet seasons in Sanur.

Interior walls in older villas often have lime plaster underneath. A good-quality vinyl-silk or matte acrylic works well there. If the wall is near a bathroom or kitchen where splashing occurs, choose a washable, mildew-resistant formulation.
Primer matters as much as topcoat. An alkali-sealing primer prevents salts migrating out of old cement render from blooming through your new colour.
bullets: Exterior: siloxane or high-build acrylic with anti-fungal additives.
Interior: vinyl-silk or matte acrylic; add a mildewcide if humidity is high.
Always use the manufacturer's recommended primer for the specific substrate (cement, brick, old paint).
Ask the supplier whether the product is tested for salt-air exposure; generic 'weatherproof' labels are not enough.

sections.h2: Surface Preparation: The Step Most People Skip
paragraphs: Eighty percent of early paint failure in Bali comes down to poor prep. Old, flaking paint must be scraped back to solid substrate. Cracks wider than 1 mm need filling with an exterior-grade flexible filler before you prime. Any visible mould or algae—common on north-facing walls that get less sun—should be killed with a diluted bleach solution, rinsed thoroughly, and allowed to dry completely before priming.

Wash the wall with clean water (PDAM tap water is fine) and a stiff brush to remove dust, bird droppings, and salt crust. Let it dry for at least 24 hours. If the plaster is crumbling or hollow-sounding when tapped, stop painting and have the render repaired first; no amount of topcoat will hold on a failing base.

Mask off windows, pool coping stones, and any electrical fixtures. If you notice exposed wiring or a damp junction box while scraping, do not continue—switch off the circuit at the breaker and call a licensed electrician before touching anything near water.
bullets: Scrape all loose paint and chalky residue; sand edges smooth.
Fill cracks > 1 mm with flexible exterior filler; let cure per product instructions.
Treat mould/algae spots, rinse, and confirm the surface is bone-dry.
Apply two thin coats of primer rather than one thick coat.
Use painter's tape and drop cloths around the pool deck and garden beds.

paragraphs: Sanur sits right on the coast, so every wall that faces east or south gets a daily dose of sea spray. This accelerates both UV fading and salt crystallisation inside porous plaster. The practical fix is twofold: choose a paint system designed for marine exposure (see above), and make sure your villa's drainage—gutters, downpipes, and ground slope away from the foundation—is working properly. Standing water against a painted wall will wick moisture up through capillary action and lift the film regardless of quality.

During painting, keep windows open to cross-ventilate interior rooms. In the dry season this dries a full interior coat in 4–6 hours. In humid months it can take over 12 hours, and rushing a second coat onto a damp first coat is the most common mistake I see.

If your villa uses a well-water supply for washing down walls before painting, check the pH; some borehole water in southern Bali is slightly acidic and can etch fresh cement render. A quick rinse with PDAM mains water after any well-water wash avoids this.

sections.h2: Realistic Timelines for a Villa Repaint
paragraphs: A typical two-storey Sanur villa (roughly 200–350 m² of exterior wall plus interiors) takes between five and ten working days from prep to final coat, assuming no structural repairs are needed. That includes scraping, filling, priming, two topcoats, and drying intervals between each layer.
Interior rooms go faster—usually one day per room including prep. Exteriors are slower because you are at the mercy of wind, sudden showers, and the need to let each coat cure fully before the next.

Budget an extra day if the plaster needs patch-repair or if you are switching from a dark colour to a light one (you may need three coats instead of two). The exact cost depends on the area, condition of the substrate, and paint grade chosen; send photos on WhatsApp and the technician will quote from what they see.
bullets: Exterior topcoats (two): 2–4 days with drying gaps.
Touch-ups and cleanup: half a day.

faq.q: Can I paint during Bali's rainy season?
faq.a: It is strongly discouraged for exterior work. Even brief rain or high humidity above 85 % prevents proper film formation and leads to peeling within weeks. If you must repaint interiors in the wet months, run a dehumidifier in the room and allow double the normal drying time between coats.

faq.q: How often should I repaint my villa's facade in Sanur?
faq.a: With a quality marine-grade system and good prep, expect to refresh the exterior every four to six years. North-facing walls that get less sun may last longer; south- and east-facing walls take more UV and salt load and can show fading sooner. Interior walls typically need a refresh every three to five years depending on traffic and humidity.

faq.q: Do I need to seal the plaster before painting?
faq.a: If the render is old, chalky, or has never been painted, yes—an alkali-sealing primer is essential to block salts and even out absorption. On previously painted surfaces in decent condition, a standard bonding primer is usually sufficient. The technician will assess this from photos of the wall texture and any existing flaking.

cta: Send a few clear photos of your walls (interior and exterior) on WhatsApp and the technician will tell you exactly what prep and paint system your villa needs before you commit to a date.
